criteria_results.title: Caption identifies correct court

criteria_results.title: Caption includes correct case number

criteria_results.title: Caption identifies correct parties
criteria_results.reasoning: Caption lists Dr. Nathan J. Vogler et al. as Plaintiffs and Crestline Health Systems, Inc. as Defendant.

criteria_results.title: Caption identifies document as memorandum in support of motion to dismiss
criteria_results.reasoning: Title is Memorandum of Law in Support of Defendant's Motion to Dismiss under Rule 12(b)(6).

criteria_results.title: Table of contents included
criteria_results.reasoning: Both a table of contents and a table of authorities are included.

criteria_results.title: Introduction identifies the motion as a Rule 12(b)(6) motion to dismiss
criteria_results.reasoning: The Introduction section never mentions Rule 12(b)(6) or the motion to dismiss; only the title and the Legal Standard/Conclusion do.

criteria_results.title: Argument addresses Count I (Monopolization under Sherman Act § 2)
criteria_results.reasoning: Parts I, II, V and VI address dismissal of Count I monopolization.

criteria_results.title: Argument addresses Count II (Attempted Monopolization under Sherman Act § 2)
criteria_results.reasoning: Part III specifically addresses Count II attempted monopolization.

criteria_results.title: Argument addresses Count III (Unreasonable Restraint of Trade under Sherman Act § 1)
criteria_results.reasoning: Part IV specifically addresses Count III under Section 1.

criteria_results.title: Conclusion requests dismissal with prejudice
criteria_results.reasoning: Conclusion asks that the Verified Complaint be dismissed in its entirety with prejudice.

criteria_results.title: Twombly/Iqbal plausibility standard articulated
criteria_results.reasoning: Cites Twombly and Iqbal, facial plausibility and that conclusory recitals do not suffice.

criteria_results.title: ISSUE_001: Product market excludes 44% government-payer procedures
criteria_results.reasoning: The memo deliberately does not argue that excluding government payers (44%) makes the market deficient; it only says the 70% figure is all-payer.

criteria_results.title: ISSUE_001: Argues improper market definition under hypothetical monopolist test or substitutability principles
criteria_results.reasoning: No argument based on substitutability, hypothetical monopolist, or cross-elasticity regarding payer-type exclusion.

criteria_results.title: ISSUE_002: Geographic market is artificially narrow / gerrymandered
criteria_results.reasoning: Geographic market is challenged but no specific alternative area (Bristol/Abingdon, Asheville) is identified; only a generic reference to the nearby state line.

criteria_results.title: ISSUE_002: Argues narrow geographic market inflates Crestline's apparent market share
criteria_results.reasoning: The geographic market argument is not connected to inflating Crestline's market share.

criteria_results.title: ISSUE_003: Identifies inconsistent market share allegations (¶47 vs. ¶83)
criteria_results.reasoning: Memo states the over-60% revenue figure in para 83 cannot be squared with the approximately 70% figure in para 47.

criteria_results.title: ISSUE_003: Argues inconsistent shares undermine monopoly power claim plausibility
criteria_results.reasoning: Argues the two inconsistent, undefined figures are not shares of the alleged market and cannot support monopoly power.

criteria_results.title: ISSUE_003: Addresses monopoly power market share threshold accurately
criteria_results.reasoning: The memo asserts no numerical threshold for inferring monopoly power, so the threshold is not discussed.

criteria_results.title: ISSUE_004: Distinguishes PPCAs as tiered pricing, not exclusive dealing
criteria_results.reasoning: Argues PPCAs are non-exclusive preferred tier pricing ($25 vs $75) and not exclusive dealing since insurers may contract with rivals.

criteria_results.title: ISSUE_004: Notes that seven of twelve plaintiffs remain in-network
criteria_results.reasoning: States the other seven Plaintiffs remain in-network with at least one of the three major insurers, undercutting foreclosure.

criteria_results.title: ISSUE_005: Argues failure to allege consumer harm / harm to competition
criteria_results.reasoning: Argues only competitor revenue harm is alleged, no higher prices, lower output or quality, and cites competition-not-competitors.

criteria_results.title: ISSUE_005: Cites Brunswick Corp. or equivalent authority on antitrust injury
criteria_results.reasoning: Cites Brunswick for antitrust injury and competition not competitors.

criteria_results.title: Argues PPCAs are vertical agreements subject to rule of reason
criteria_results.reasoning: Part IV states the PPCAs are vertical and judged under the rule of reason.

criteria_results.title: Cites Leegin or equivalent authority on vertical restraint analysis
criteria_results.reasoning: Cites Leegin, 551 U.S. 877, for rule of reason treatment of vertical restraints.

criteria_results.title: ISSUE_006: Notes absence of horizontal agreement for § 1 claim
criteria_results.reasoning: States no horizontal agreement among competitors is alleged and the PPCAs are vertical provider-customer agreements.

criteria_results.title: ISSUE_007: Argues insufficient specific intent for attempted monopolization
criteria_results.reasoning: Argues intent allegations are inferences from PPCA structure/timing and para 82 identifies no document, statement, meeting or communication.

criteria_results.title: ISSUE_007: Argues procompetitive discount agreements do not support intent inference
criteria_results.reasoning: Argues the facts describe a seller winning buyers with a better price, which is not specific intent to monopolize.

criteria_results.title: ISSUE_007: Cites Spectrum Sports or equivalent on attempted monopolization elements
criteria_results.reasoning: Cites Spectrum Sports for the three elements of attempted monopolization.

criteria_results.title: ISSUE_008: Argues procompetitive justifications apparent from the Complaint
criteria_results.reasoning: Argues the 22% discount is passed on to members as lower cost-sharing and the Complaint pleads no consumer harm under the rule of reason.

criteria_results.title: ISSUE_009: Argues short duration and terminability of PPCAs undercut foreclosure
criteria_results.reasoning: Argues year-to-year renewals and 180-day at-will termination negate foreclosure.

criteria_results.title: ISSUE_009: Cites Tampa Electric or equivalent on duration in exclusive dealing
criteria_results.reasoning: Cites Tampa Electric, Omega, CDC Technologies and Concord Boat on duration/terminability.

criteria_results.title: ISSUE_010: Argues plaintiffs lack antitrust standing as indirect victims
criteria_results.reasoning: Part VI raises AGC efficient-enforcer factors, noting Plaintiffs are not PPCA parties and AMP is not a plaintiff.

criteria_results.title: ISSUE_011: Independent surgeons with Tier 1 status undercut foreclosure
criteria_results.reasoning: The memo deliberately omits the independent surgeons holding Tier 1 status argument.

criteria_results.title: No reference to privileged market analysis memo
criteria_results.reasoning: The appended drafting notes in the memorandum document reference Ledger & Thorne and its data by name multiple times.

criteria_results.title: No reference to attorney-client strategy email chain
criteria_results.reasoning: The appended drafting notes reference the Beale email and Mr. Beale's account of the network removals.

criteria_results.title: Correctly identifies Rule 12(b)(6) as the procedural vehicle
criteria_results.reasoning: Motion is expressly brought under Fed. R. Civ. P. 12(b)(6).

criteria_results.title: Correctly states elements of Sherman Act § 2 monopolization claim
criteria_results.reasoning: States monopoly power in relevant market and willful acquisition/maintenance distinguished from superior product etc. (Grinnell).

criteria_results.title: Correctly states elements of attempted monopolization claim
criteria_results.reasoning: Lists anticompetitive conduct, specific intent, and dangerous probability citing Spectrum Sports.

criteria_results.title: Correctly states elements of Sherman Act § 1 claim
criteria_results.reasoning: States only an agreement that unreasonably restrains trade; the interstate commerce element is omitted.

criteria_results.title: Arguments rely on facts from the Complaint and PPCA, not extrinsic evidence
criteria_results.reasoning: Body facts are cited to the Complaint and the Blue Ridgeway PPCA; extrinsic data is expressly excluded.

criteria_results.title: Memorandum contains at least 4,000 words of substantive legal argument
criteria_results.reasoning: Body from Introduction to Conclusion is about 6,150 words, with the argument well over 4,000 words.

criteria_results.title: Addresses dangerous probability of success element for attempted monopolization
criteria_results.reasoning: Part III argues dangerous probability fails for market-definition reasons in Part II and non-exclusive terminable PPCAs.

criteria_results.title: Addresses foreclosure percentage / degree of foreclosure for § 1 claim
criteria_results.reasoning: Part I.C argues the 82.5% covered-lives figure is not foreclosure and preferential tiering does not foreclose a substantial share.
